title: How Much Does It Cost to Install Hardwood on Stairs in Kirkland?
meta: Hardwood on stairs in Kirkland costs $125 per stair in labor at Wills Flooring, plus treads and material. See what drives the price, with real examples.

blocks.lead: Wills Flooring installs hardwood on stairs for $125 per stair in Kirkland, labor only, with the treads, risers and nosings quoted separately as material.
blocks.detail: A typical 13-stair Kirkland split-level runs $1,625 in labor. Add the main floor at $3.25 per sq ft and most whole-project quotes land between $4,000 and $7,000 before material.

blocks.html: The question usually arrives like this: "We are replacing the carpet on the main floor of our Rose Hill split-level with hardwood, and the stairs are carpeted too. What does it cost to do the stairs?" Kirkland has a lot of 1970s to 1990s two-story and split-level homes in Rose Hill, Finn Hill and Juanita where the staircase is the first thing you see from the front door. Here is how we price it, what the per-stair number includes, and where the surprises hide.

items.title: Included in the labor
items.text: Tearing off old carpet, pad and tack strip, pulling staples, checking each stringer and tread for squeaks, installing the new tread, riser and nosing, scribing to the wall on closed stairs, and setting the return on open-sided treads. One price per stair, straight or pie-shaped.

items.title: Quoted as material
items.text: Solid stair treads, risers, stair nosings and any landing flooring. A stair tread is a thick, one-piece board, not floor planks glued together, and it costs more per stair than the flooring in the room. We bring tread samples in your species and color so the match is real.

items.title: Landings are square footage
items.text: A mid-run landing on a split-level or an L-shaped staircase is floored like a room and billed at $3.25 per sq ft, with its own nosing at the edge. A 3 × 4 ft landing is about 12 sq ft, so it adds very little, but it needs to be measured and counted rather than guessed.

items.title: Not in the number
items.text: Painting the risers if you want white risers, new balusters or handrails, and structural fixes to a stringer that has split or pulled away. We flag those at the estimate so the written quote is the whole job, not the starting point.

blocks.text: What changes the price on a Kirkland staircase

head: Situation
Effect on cost
Why
rows: Closed stairs, walls on both sides
Treads are cut square and scribed. The most common stair in Juanita and Totem Lake two-stories.
Open on one side with a return
The exposed end needs a mitered return nosing, which is an extra piece of tread stock per step.
Each winder is cut from a wider tread blank. Three winders can use as much stock as five straight treads.
Builder stairs from the 1980s and 90s often have particleboard treads. We cap or replace them; that is the whole point of the job.
Base labor plus a riser trim
When the new tread sits on top of the old one, each riser is cut a little shorter. Rarely a problem, but it is why we measure every step.
Screwing down loose treads is included. Rebuilding a stringer is carpentry and is priced on its own.

blocks.text: Should the stairs match the floor exactly?

blocks.html: In Kirkland, yes, almost always. Buyers on the Eastside expect the staircase to read as part of the floor, and a mismatched stair is the kind of thing a Houghton or Bridle Trails listing photo makes obvious. Matching is easy with prefinished engineered floors when the same manufacturer makes stair nosings and treads in the same color. It is harder with site-finished floors, which is where unfinished treads sanded and finished with the floor come in: same wood, same stain, same finish, on the same day.

a.title: Choose these when
items: The floor is solid hardwood or a site-finished install
You want a one-piece tread with a rounded bullnose
The stairs are open on one side and need a returned end
You want stairs that can be sanded and refinished in 15 years

b.title: Choose these when
items: The floor is a prefinished engineered plank with a matching nosing
Budget matters more than a one-piece look
The existing treads are sound and you are covering them
You are fine with a visible seam between nosing and plank

blocks.text: When hardwood on stairs is the wrong call

items.html: Big dogs and steep stairs. Hardwood stairs are slippery for older dogs. A stair runner solves it, but it adds cost and hides the wood. Carpeted stairs with a hardwood main floor is an honest compromise many Kirkland families choose.
Toddlers and a rental. If the house is a rental or you have a crawler, carpet on the stairs is safer and cheaper to replace. Do the main floor in hardwood and revisit the stairs later.

The stairs are out of code. Old Kirkland stairs with 7 in treads or uneven risers cannot be fixed with new hardwood. Adding thickness to the tread without adjusting the bottom and top step creates a trip hazard. We check rise and run before we quote.
Vinyl plank is going on the floor. If the main floor is LVP, put LVP on the stairs at $100 per stair rather than paying for hardwood treads that will not match.

blocks.title: One thing to check before you sign anything:
blocks.text: Ask whether the per-stair price includes tearing out the carpet and pulling the staples. Some quotes leave that as a separate demolition line, and on 13 stairs it changes the total noticeably. Ours includes it.
How to get a firm number instead of a range

items: Count the stairs and note which ones are pie-shaped or open on a side. That is 80 percent of the quote.
Pick the floor first. The tread, riser and nosing options follow from the floor you choose, and so does the material price.
Decide on riser color early. Painting is easier before the treads go in.
Book the free estimate. We bring tread samples, measure each step, check the stringers, and write the price on the spot.

faq.q: How much does it cost to install hardwood on 13 stairs?
faq.a: At Wills Flooring's published rate, 13 stairs cost 13 × $125 = $1,625 in installation labor. The treads, risers and nosings are quoted separately as material, and the number depends on species, whether the ends are open and how many steps are pie-shaped. We quote the full figure at the free estimate.

faq.q: Is hardwood on stairs more expensive than on the floor?
faq.a: Per square foot, yes. A single stair is roughly 3 sq ft of surface but takes far longer than 3 sq ft of floor because every tread is fitted, scribed and nosed by hand. That is why stairs are priced per step at $125 rather than at the $3.25 per sq ft floor rate.

faq.q: Can you put hardwood on stairs over the existing treads?
faq.a: Often, yes. If the old treads are solid and level, a new tread and riser can cap them. The added thickness shifts the bottom and top step by a fraction of an inch, so we check the rise at both ends first. Particleboard treads under carpet are usually replaced instead.

faq.q: Do the risers have to be wood?
faq.a: No. Painted white risers with wood treads are the most popular combination in Kirkland right now. We install a paint-grade riser and you or your painter finish it. If you want wood risers to match the treads, the material cost goes up slightly.

faq.q: How long does it take to install hardwood on stairs?
faq.a: A straight 13-stair run is usually one day, sometimes into a second morning if the stairs are open-sided with returns. Winders and split-level layouts add time. If the stairs are site-finished with the floor, add the sanding and finishing days on top.

faq.q: Does the 500 sq ft minimum apply to a stairs-only job?
faq.a: Stairs are priced per step, not by square foot, so a staircase on its own is quoted at $125 per stair plus material. Most stair jobs in Kirkland come with a main floor anyway, and the floor is where the 500 sq ft minimum applies.
